laws.rule: Foreign tourists over 12 pay a USD 200 Galápagos protected-areas entry fee on arrival at Baltra or San Cristóbal (USD 100 under 12) and need a USD 20 Transit Control Card bought before flying.

The Galápagos National Park and Marine Reserve visit rules say to keep 2 metres from wildlife (cameras included), not to touch or feed animals, not to remove anything from the ecosystem, and not to bring in outside plants or animals.
The park's visit rules say: do not use drones. Take photos without flash; professional filming needs authorisation.

Visitors walk on marked trails and visit protected areas with a specialised (naturalist) guide. Camping is only in designated sites with prior authorisation. Tourism services must be authorised ones; motorised watercraft, submarines and air tourism are not to be used.
In the park's visit areas, do not smoke, drink alcohol or light campfires.
